cover.question: What did he never finish?
cover.name: PARMIGIANINO
cover.answered_by: The whole altarpiece: he died in 1540 with it unfinished; St Francis beside St Jerome is only one painted foot, and the step's inscription says fate prevented him from completing it

facts.claim: Madonna with the Long Neck, Parmigianino (1503–1540), 1534–1540; commissioned 1534 by Elena Baiardi Tagliaferri for Santa Maria dei Servi, Parma
The Child is 'extremely large for a baby' and 'lies precariously on Mary's lap as if about to fall at any moment'
The small figure with a scroll at lower right is St Jerome; Gombrich: so reduced in size that he 'hardly reaches the Madonna's knee'
Beside St Jerome, St Francis was left unfinished: only one foot is painted

Parmigianino died in 1540 leaving it unfinished; installed on the altar two years later with the inscription FATO PRAEVENTUS F. MAZZOLI PARMENSIS ABSOLVERE NEQUIVIT ('Adverse destiny prevented Francesco Mazzola from Parma from completing this work')
The neck: the Madonna has 'a neck like that of a swan' (Gombrich); the column beside her may allude to the hymn line 'Collum tuum ut columna' (Your neck is like a column)
Bought by Grand Prince Ferdinando de' Medici in 1698; in the Uffizi since 1948

caption:
Her neck is the least strange thing in this painting.

Look at the baby: far too big for a baby, and lying on Mary's lap as if about to slide off. Look at the tiny saint with a scroll at lower right, St Jerome: as Gombrich put it, he hardly reaches the Madonna's knee. Now look beside him: one foot, and no saint. St Francis was supposed to stand there.

Parmigianino started this altarpiece in 1534 for a chapel in Parma. He died in 1540 with it still in his studio. When it went up on the altar two years later, an inscription was added on the step: "FATO PRAEVENTUS F. MAZZOLI PARMENSIS ABSOLVERE NEQUIVIT" — fate prevented Francesco Mazzola of Parma from completing it.

P.S. The column beside her may echo an old hymn to Mary: "Your neck is like a column."
